findings.text: The regex `[0-9;]+m` requires at least one digit/semicolon, so the common reset code `\033[m` (empty parameters) will not be matched or removed, leaving unescaped ESC characters in XML output.

The regex only matches ANSI codes ending in 'm' (SGR color codes), but ignores other valid ANSI sequences like `\033[2J` (clear screen) or `\033[H` (cursor home), leaving those ESC characters unescaped in XML.

The while loop reuses BASH_REMATCH[0] from the condition check in the substitution, but if the substitution fails to remove the match (e.g., special characters in the match), the loop will infinite-loop on the same match.

2.reason: The matched string only contains ESC, [, digits, ;, and m — none of which (given the absence of a closing ]) cause the glob-pattern substitution to fail, so no infinite loop occurs.
